messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `testUnion()` verifies that the union of two XPath queries returns the nodes in document order, which is critical for correct XPath string value evaluation. The current bug report highlights that the core union operation does not sort the resulting nodes according to document order, leading to incorrect string values when converting a node-set to string — the string-value should come from the first node in document order.

The test asserts that the union of two disjoint node selections (e.g. `/vendor[1]/contact[4] | /vendor[1]/contact[1]`) returns a result where the string-value corresponds to the node that appears earlier in the document (`contact[1]` named "John"), regardless of the order of unioned node paths.

While the exact class responsible for the union operation (`UnionPathIterator`) could not be found in the code base, the core issue relates to the behavior of union node collections — the nodes must be sorted in document order after union. The symptom in the report (getting "bvalue" instead of "avalue") confirms that the union operation returns nodes in the order of the union expressions rather than document order.

From the snippet of `DOMNodePointer.getValue()`, we observe the string value extraction depends on the node's document text and does not itself sort nodes, meaning sorting responsibility lies where nodes are collected for union queries.

In summary, the root cause is that the union operation for XPath node-sets does not sort the resulting nodes by document order, causing failures when string conversion expects nodes in document order. The fix likely requires ensuring that the union of nodes is followed by proper sorting before returning results.

The recent bug report about namespace prefix issues is unrelated and does not impact this failure.

This diagnosis matches the failing test behavior and the issue report description directly.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
